Classic Independence Day Baked Beans

Served at: Independence Day (United States)

Serves 8-10Prep 20 min (plus overnight bean soaking)Cook 3-4 hours

These classic baked beans are a quintessential side dish for any Fourth of July barbecue or picnic. Slow-cooked to perfection with a rich, sweet, and savory sauce, they embody the comforting flavors of American summer celebrations. They're a beloved staple, offering a hearty and flavorful contrast to grilled meats and other festive fare.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450g) dried navy beans
  • 6 slices thick-cut bacon, diced
  • 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 cup (120 mL) dark molasses
  • 1/4 cup (50g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 mL) ketchup
  • 2 tablespoons (30 mL) apple cider vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) dry mustard powder
  • 1 teaspoon (5 mL) salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 mL) black pepper
  • 4 cups (960 mL) water or reserved bean cooking liquid

Method

  1. Rinse the dried navy beans thoroughly. Place them in a large bowl, cover with at least 3 inches (7.5 cm) of cold water, and soak overnight (8-12 hours). Alternatively, use the quick-soak method: bring beans and water to a boil, boil for 2 minutes, remove from heat, cover, and let stand for 1 hour.
  2. Drain the soaked beans and transfer them to a large pot. Cover with fresh water by about 2 inches (5 cm). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until beans are tender but still hold their shape. Drain, reserving 1 cup (240 mL) of the cooking liquid.
  3. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C).
  4. In a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
  5. Add the chopped onion to the bacon fat in the pot and cook over medium heat until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  6. Stir in the molasses, brown sugar, ketchup, apple cider vinegar, dry mustard, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine.
  7. Add the cooked beans to the pot and stir to coat them evenly with the sauce. Pour in 3 cups (720 mL) of fresh water or the reserved bean cooking liquid. The liquid should just cover the beans.
  8. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer on the stovetop. Once simmering, cover the pot and transfer it to the preheated oven.
  9. Bake for 3 to 4 hours, stirring every hour, until the beans are very tender and the sauce has thickened to your desired consistency. If the beans seem too dry, add more water or reserved bean liquid as needed.
  10. During the last 30 minutes of baking, stir in the cooked crispy bacon. If you prefer, you can sprinkle some bacon on top for garnish just before serving.
  11. Serve hot alongside your favorite grilled meats and other Independence Day dishes.

Tips

  • For a quicker version, use 3 (15-ounce / 425g) cans of great northern or navy beans, rinsed and drained, skipping the soaking and simmering steps. Reduce the initial water added to 1-2 cups (240-480 mL) as canned beans are already cooked.
  • Add a diced bell pepper (green or red) along with the onion for extra flavor and color. A pinch of cayenne pepper can also add a subtle kick.
  • These beans can be made a day ahead and reheated gently on the stovetop or in the oven, allowing the flavors to meld even further. Add a splash of water if they've thickened too much.
